title: From Toys.com to Toys “R” Us
lede: Incorporation to liquidation took six years; the store itself was open for three and a half. Filter by thread.

events.title: Toys.com
events.text: The company is incorporated in Delaware as Toys.com.

events.title: eToys Inc.
events.text: After a brief spell as eToys.com Inc., the company takes the name eToys Inc.; Idealab holds its founding shares.

events.title: Open for business
events.text: eToys begins selling on its website.

events.title: First full year
events.text: In the year to March 1999: $30.0M of sales, a $28.6M net loss.

events.title: The IPO
events.text: 8.32 million shares at $20; first-day close $76.56; market value $7.78 billion.

events.title: A $189.6M loss
events.text: Year to March 2000: $151.0M of sales, $55.5M of advertising, 1.9 million customers.

events.title: Preferred stock
events.text: eToys sells $100M of convertible preferred stock, which converts into ever more shares as the price falls.

events.title: The warning
events.text: Holiday sales will be $120M–$130M, not $210M–$240M; cash will last to about March 31.

events.title: 700 job notices
events.text: About 700 of roughly 1,000 staff are given notice; two warehouses and the UK site close.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: eToys files in Delaware, owing about $274M, and closes its website that night.

events.title: Inventory sold
events.text: KB Toys buys most of the stock for about $5.4M.

events.title: The name sold
events.text: KB Toys pays nearly $3.4M for the name, website and software.

events.title: Liquidation plan
events.text: The plan for EBC I, Inc., formerly eToys, takes effect; the companies are to be dissolved.

events.title: Creditors v. Goldman
events.text: New York’s Court of Appeals lets the fiduciary-duty claim over the IPO price go forward.

events.title: Toys “R” Us
events.text: Toys “R” Us buys eToys.com from the bankrupt Parent Company.
